name: depth-repeat-1

message.content:
The three marker values are:
1. amber-violet-731
2. birch-cobalt-482
3. cedar-silver-956

The rain did not fall so much as it descended, a heavy, gray curtain that erased the horizon and turned the world into a study in monochrome. It was the kind of rain that smelled of wet stone and old iron, a scent that clung to the back of the throat and reminded one of things long forgotten. In this deluge, the bridge stood as the only anchor in a dissolving reality. It was an ancient structure, built from granite blocks that had been smoothed by centuries of wind and water, their surfaces slick and dark with the relentless downpour. The arches, elegant and severe, spanned the churning river below, which had swollen into a brown, frothing beast, hungry for the banks it had long since claimed.

Walking across the bridge was a solitary figure, their silhouette barely distinguishable from the mist that clung to the stone railings. The cobblestones beneath their feet were treacherous, slick with moss and rainwater, reflecting the dim, ambient light of the sky. But it was not the sky that provided the most striking illumination. Along the length of the bridge, suspended from iron hooks that had rusted into the color of dried blood, hung a row of lanterns. They were old things, crafted from brass and glass, their panes clouded by age and soot. Yet, as the twilight deepened into night, they were lit, one by one, by an unseen hand.

The light they cast was not the harsh, white glare of modern electricity, but a warm, amber glow that seemed to breathe. Each lantern held a flame that danced within its glass cage, fighting against the drafts that whistled through the bridge’s arches. The light spilled onto the wet stones, creating pools of gold that shimmered and distorted in the rain. Where the droplets struck the light, they became tiny
